verdict.rationale: Fivetran's REST API is URL-path versioned under /v1 with a published OpenAPI V1 spec. Its dated changelog records deprecations with sunset dates (e.g. May 1, 2025), so it delivers versioning and per-change deprecation notices. However, the evidence says there is no standalone versioning or breaking-change policy page, so the 'documented deprecation policy' half of the story is only met in practice, not as a formal policy. Missing for 10: a formal documented deprecation/breaking-change policy with guaranteed notice windows, any multi-version history beyond v1, and independent corroboration of how deprecations are handled.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: The REST API publishes dated release notes recording changes and deprecations with sunset dates
The API is URL-path versioned under /v1
The spec file itself downloads as OpenAPI 3.0.1 (info version "v1"), covering the /v1 REST API.
